observations: Photo 0 shows a white industrial sewing machine setup on a table with a long bed; there is a brand badge on the machine head that reads “Emel”.
Photo 0 shows a control box with indicator lights (green/red) on the right side of the table.
Photo 0 shows a measuring tape hanging down in front of the machine; the machine appears intact but there is no visible running/operation.
Photo 1 shows the same machine from a wider angle; the “Emel” badge is visible on the head.
Photo 1 shows a label on the machine body that appears to include “EMEL” and possibly a model/series, but the exact model number is not readable in the image.
No clear close-up of the motor/spec plate, no clear view of stitch type/capability, and no proof the machine is currently working.

claims.claim: 1 year used industrial machine working perfectly
claims.evidence: Photos show the machine present but do not show it running, stitching, or any test results; usage age is not verifiable from the images.

risks.risk: Machine may not be functional under load (timing, motor health, clutch/drive issues). Photos cannot confirm operation.
risks.proof: A short video of the machine running and stitching a sample fabric/cloth (show feed moving, needle cycling, and a finished seam).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as needs service/untested).

risks.risk: Wrong model/spec for the buyer’s intended work (industrial machine type/capability not readable).
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the model/serial plate and the label on the machine body (sharp text), plus a photo of the presser foot/needle type.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic industrial sewing machine with unknown specs (worst case: limited capability).

risks.risk: Electrical/control issues (control box indicators may not reflect real performance; wiring/foot pedal condition unknown).
risks.proof: Video showing power on, foot pedal press, and motor speed change; close-up of wiring connections and foot pedal.
risks.if_unproven: Price as electrical/control not guaranteed (worst case: may require electrical repair).

risks.risk: Missing accessories/consumables (needles, bobbins, presser feet, belts, manuals) affecting usability and cost to get started.
risks.proof: Photo list of included accessories laid out on the table (needles, bobbins, presser feet, power cable, pedal, any manuals).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming minimal/no accessories included (worst case: buyer must source parts).

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up of the model/serial plate text on the machine body (so the exact model can be identified).
Send a short video of the machine stitching (needle moving + fabric feed) and the seam result.
Show the foot pedal and control box in operation (power on + pedal press + speed change).
List and photograph all included accessories (needles, bobbins, presser feet, belts/cables, pedal, manual if any).
response.reason: The photos identify it as an Emel industrial sewing machine, but they do not prove it is working or confirm the exact model/spec. Since the seller’s “working perfectly” and “1 year used” cannot be verified remotely, the correct next step is to request operation and model proof before pricing confidently.
